name: Miles HVAC Playbook
label: HVAC
summary: Win the first hot and first cold weeks with speed, fill the shoulder seasons with tune-ups and memberships, and sell replacements on monthly payment. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: Intro
lines: Win the first hot and first cold weeks with speed, fill the shoulder seasons with tune-ups and memberships, and sell replacements on monthly payment. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: 1. At a glance
lines: Emergency (no heat / no AC) + planned replacement + recurring maintenance
System replacement; repair; tune-up as front door
$[XX] pre-season tune-up (21-point) or diagnostic credited to repair
Comfort club membership: 2 tune-ups/yr, priority service, 10–15% off repairs
New systems use A2L refrigerants (R-454B or R-32); R-410A service refrigerant is getting more expensive; the federal 25C heat pump credit no longer applies to 2026 installs

sections.title: 2. Seasonality by region
lines: Launch AC tune-ups late March; furnace tune-ups late August
Off-season reactivation converts at about half the in-season rate, so time sends to the shoulder before each peak.

sections.title: 3. Location signals (add to ZIP score)
lines: Median year built: systems 12–15+ years old are replacement-ready.
Cooling and heating degree days for the ZIP (sizes demand per season).
Fuel mix: gas-heat ZIPs vs all-electric (heat pump) ZIPs need different creative.
Owner-occupied share and income; financing-first where ticket ÷ income is high.
Utility or state rebates available in the ZIP (federal credits are gone; local rebates are now the incentive story).

sections.title: 4. Demographics and audiences
lines: Emergency buyer: any homeowner, decides in minutes; wins on answer speed, same-day slots, and reviews.
Replacement buyer: homeowner 40–70 with an older system; compares 2–3 quotes; wants payment, warranty, and comfort.
Seniors: safety and reliability messaging (no-heat risk); offer priority membership.
Audiences: past customers by equipment age; homeowners in scored ZIPs; retargeting to estimate-not-sold.

Load with the Audience framework in the Master Template. Emergency segments get no income or homeowner filter and start at 25+; planned segments use the filters below. Ages are starting points: Miles tightens them from closed-won CRM data after 30 booked jobs.
preferred, not required (landlords and renters call too)
Search + LSA: repair terms; no demographic exclusions; run nights/weekends only if phones answered
Search: replacement/heat pump terms; observe Homeowners, age; exclude Renters
past repair customers with equipment 12+ yrs old
past customers first; then high-score ZIPs
custom audience of past customers + lookalike
Customer Match; Demand Gen to past customers
Exclude in every segment: customers from the last 12 months (except retention campaigns), open leads and estimates, employees, out-of-area ZIPs.

sections.title: 5. Offer stack
lines: $[XX] tune-up through [date] or diagnostic credited to repair
$[X] off a new system + financing from $[X]/mo
Air quality (filtration, UV), smart thermostat, duct sealing, surge protection
Comfort club: 2 tune-ups, priority, repair discount, no overtime fees
Filter reminder; pre-season check; membership renewal with "you saved $X"
Same-day no-heat / no-AC; no discount, sell speed

Repair-vs-replace angle: systems on R-410A still get serviced, but refrigerant leaks are getting costlier; age + leak + repair cost is the replacement conversation. Never say R-410A systems must be replaced.

sections.title: 6. Channels and campaign build
lines: Google Search + LSA carry emergency demand; split "AC repair", "furnace repair", "AC/furnace replacement", "heat pump".
Negatives: jobs, HVAC school, DIY, parts, filters, window units, car AC.
Meta: retargeting and tune-up/membership offers to past customers and lookalikes; replacement financing creative.
Dayparting: keep emergency campaigns running nights and weekends only if phones are answered.

sections.title: 7. Triggers Miles watches
lines: Forecast ≥ 90°F (or local top 10% heat) within 5 days
Raise AC repair budget, push same-day slots, pause tune-up ads
Raise heating repair budget; no-heat landing page
Tune-up campaign + reactivation to past customers by equipment age

sections.title: 8. After the job and retention
lines: Every repair: offer membership on site; thank-you coupon for next tune-up; honest review ask to everyone.
Every install: record equipment, install date and warranty in CRM; 30-day comfort check; annual tune-up reminder at month 11.
Equipment-age reactivation (6 touches, 21 days) from the Master Template.

sections.title: 9. Compliance and watch-outs
lines: Don't advertise federal tax credits for 2026 installs; check state and utility rebates before using any rebate claim.
Refrigerant claims must be accurate: no "R-410A is banned" scare copy.
Membership terms must list exclusions; never imply it covers excluded repairs.

sections.title: 10. Deploy checklist
lines: ☐ Confirm services (gas, heat pump, ductless, commercial) and brands carried
☐ Map region and set seasonal calendar; set heat and cold triggers
☐ Load tune-up, replacement financing, and membership offers with real terms
☐ Build Search + LSA by service, Meta retargeting, replacement and repair landing pages
☐ Import past customers with equipment age; schedule pre-season reactivation
☐ Turn on missed-call text-back (critical for HVAC), estimate follow-up, post-job and membership automations
Sources: 25C heat pump credit ended (Budget Heating, citing IRS) · refrigerant rules (Kele, 2026) · R-410A service vs new equipment (gcn.com) · seasonal timing from the HVAC reactivation sequence.
